<reflection>
After three experiments, the cumulative negative log-likelihood (NLL) values show that M6 and M8 remain the best-fitting models, with nearly identical NLLs. M7 is slightly worse, followed closely by M2, M10, M15, M1, and others. The differences among the top candidates are still small, indicating that more discriminatory power is needed. The previous experiments varied substrate and catalyst concentrations but always started with zero product. Introducing initial product is a new dimension that can probe reversibility, product inhibition, and deactivation pathways. This could help distinguish between mechanisms that are otherwise similar in their substrate and catalyst dependencies.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
I propose an experiment with the same substrate and catalyst concentrations as the first run (S=2.0 M, cat=0.01 M) but with an initial product concentration of 0.2 M. This condition tests the effect of product on the reaction kinetics. Mechanisms with reversible steps (e.g., M1, M2) will exhibit a slower net forward rate due to the reverse reaction. Mechanisms with product inhibition or product-induced deactivation (e.g., M12, M17) may show stronger suppression of activity. Activation mechanisms (M6, M8) might be less affected if the activation step is irreversible and not product-sensitive. By comparing this run with the first run (which had the same S and cat but no initial product), we can directly observe the product's influence. This design avoids extreme conditions and provides information that simultaneously discriminates among multiple top candidates based on their sensitivity to product.
</hypothesis>
